question: What are the most influential papers on RNA interference? Return 5 with DOIs and citation counts.
final_text:
I also noticed the earlier search returned two highly relevant papers not captured in the second query — the Drosha/microRNA paper and the Dicer/bidentate ribonuclease paper. Let me now compile the best 5 core RNAi papers from all results, replacing the off-topic CRISPR Cpf1 entry with the more relevant ones identified earlier.

{"answer":"The most influential papers on RNA interference (RNAi), ranked by citation count on OpenAIRE, are: (1) the landmark 1998 Fire & Mello Nature paper demonstrating potent gene silencing by dsRNA in C. elegans (Nobel Prize work, 13,226 citations); (2) the 2001 Elbashir et al. paper showing 21-nt siRNA duplexes mediate RNAi in mammalian cells (8,557 citations); (3) the 2001 Bernstein et al. paper identifying Dicer as the bidentate ribonuclease that initiates RNAi (4,146 citations); (4) Hannon's 2002 Nature review comprehensively covering the RNAi mechanism (3,724 citations); and (5) the 2003 Nature paper by Lee et al. identifying Drosha as the nuclear RNase III that initiates microRNA processing, a key part of the RNAi pathway (4,415 citations).","citations":[{"doi":"10.1038/35888","title":"Potent and specific genetic interference by double-stranded RNA in Caenorhabditis elegans","citation_count":13226},{"doi":"10.1038/35078107","title":"Duplexes of 21-nucleotide RNAs mediate RNA interference in cultured mammalian cells","citation_count":8557},{"doi":"10.1038/nature01957","title":"The nuclear RNase III Drosha initiates microRNA processing","citation_count":4415},{"doi":"10.1038/35053110","title":"Role for a bidentate ribonuclease in the initiation step of RNA interference","citation_count":4146},{"doi":"10.1038/418244a","title":"RNA interference","citation_count":3724}]}
